To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Hypoxia-inducibale factor 1 ( HIF-1 ) activation during tumor progression is a key step in tumor growth, angiogenesis, invasion, metastasis and chemoresistance.
HIF-1 is a key factor in tumoral progression.
HIF-1 is activated in many types of tumors and plays a key role in tumor progression by regulating the expression of a wide range of genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HIF-2alpha and HIF-3alpha isoforms in the regulation of HIF-3beta and HIF-1beta gene expression.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of HIF- 1 activation and its role in tumor progression.
the identification of new molecular and cellular pathways that could be used to develop novel therapeutic strategies against cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIF-1 is a major regulator of tumor progression.
HIF-1 is not a tumor-promoting or -suppressive factor but rather that it is an adaptive response to hypoxia and that its activation in tumors is a consequence of the hypoxic microenvironment.
HIF-1 is an essential factor in the progression of cancer and that it is a potential therapeutic target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF-1 is an important factor in tumor progression.
HIF-1 is a key factor in tumoral progression.
HIF-1 is a master regulator of tumor progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIF-1 is not a mere hypoxic stress marker but is a key player in tumor progression and is therefore a potential therapeutic target.
